frames.label: Invasion
frames.headline: The North Korean invasion opens across the 38th Parallel.
frames.summary: Seven assault divisions, armored forces, and supporting formations cross into the Republic of Korea. The line shown is the prewar boundary and opening contact zone, not a stabilized battlefield front.

frames.label: Seoul Falls
frames.headline: Seoul falls as the ROK defense fragments south of the Han.
frames.summary: The western defense is no longer a continuous line. North Korean columns enter Seoul while other axes press through the central mountains and down the east coast.

frames.label: Suwon–Wonju–Samcheok
frames.headline: The invasion reaches the Suwon–Wonju–Samcheok alignment.
frames.summary: The western thrust breaks the Suwon delay and presses toward Osan. The former NKPA 7th Division approaches Wonju, while east-coast forces continue south toward Samcheok. Task Force Smith prepares north of Osan.

frames.label: Taejon Lost
frames.headline: Taejon falls; the delaying battle moves toward the southeast.
frames.summary: UN and ROK forces continue trading ground for time. North Korean columns push beyond the Kum River and threaten the approaches to Taegu, while the eastern advance pressures the Andong–Yongdok region.

frames.label: Pusan Perimeter
frames.headline: The UN defense contracts behind the Naktong into the Pusan Perimeter.
frames.summary: The southeastern lodgment becomes the final defensive position. Taegu, Pohang, the Naktong crossings, and the southwestern approach to Pusan are all under pressure.

frames.label: Inchon
frames.headline: The Inchon landing opens a second front behind the North Korean armies.
frames.summary: The Pusan Perimeter still exists, but the strategic geometry has changed. X Corps lands at Inchon while Eighth Army prepares to break out from the southeast.

frames.label: Seoul Recaptured
frames.headline: Seoul is recaptured and North Korean forces retreat toward the parallel.
frames.summary: The Inchon force and the breakout from the perimeter collapse the North Korean rear. Fighter-bombers return permanently to Taegu as the air-base system expands northward.

frames.label: Across the Parallel
frames.headline: UN forces cross the 38th Parallel as Korean airfields reopen behind them.
frames.summary: Pohang is back in USAF use, and support organizations move into Suwon. The operational front has returned to the prewar boundary and is beginning to move into North Korea.

airfields.name: Itazuke Air Base
airfields.note: Primary Black Scorpions base and dependable F-80 operating location throughout the opening campaign.

airfields.name: Pusan West
airfields.note: Logistics and transport gateway; the only initially surfaced Korean runway reported capable of handling an F-80.

airfields.name: Taegu No. 1
airfields.note: Central tactical-air-control and staging field; early runway remained marginal for advanced aircraft.

states.detail: Joint Operations Center and tactical control
Flying units evacuated; refuel/rearm staging continues

airfields.name: Pohangdong
airfields.note: First South Korean base to host a USAF fighter group; repeatedly threatened during the perimeter battle.

states.detail: First USAF fighter group based in Korea
Area recovered; field not yet a sustained base

airfields.name: Taejon
airfields.note: Useful for command and light operations before the city fell; not a dependable opening-war fighter base.

airfields.name: Pusan East
airfields.note: Secure perimeter fighter base as the southeastern airfield network matured.

airfields.name: Suwon
airfields.note: Forward jet-capable objective south of Seoul; lost during the opening retreat and reopened after the counteroffensive.

airfields.name: Kimpo
airfields.note: Major Seoul-area airfield; captured in June, retaken after Inchon, and rebuilt for forward operations.
